content:
Earlier this July, Apple updated its TestFlight app with a basic search function. While you might think such a simple update would be welcomed, the same TestFlight update introduced a rather annoying bug for many users.

Personally, I wasn't bothered by this seemingly obvious bug. So I figured the TestFlight update was a small but meaningful step.

Sometimes, a small change can have a big impact. That's especially true for users with a large backlog of pre-release software betas, following Apple's latest TestFlight update. Apple just updated TestFlight across iPhone, iPad, and Mac. The new version 4.3 added "a search field to quickly find apps".

In hindsight, I did notice something odd, which I noted at the end of the article (but got the assessment backwards):

I think the reason I missed this bug was that over the years I've built up a backlog of TestFlight betas that survived the consolidation of my separate iCloud and App Store Apple accounts last year. It was a hassle, but worth it for me.

Anyway, John Vorhees at MacStories noticed the TestFlight app bug:

So you can imagine my excitement when I saw Zac Hall over at 9to5Mac write about TestFlight getting a search field. I thought to myself, "It's about time." I immediately stopped what I was doing to update the app. […] Unfortunately, there's a rather large "but" to this story. Previously, TestFlight betas were listed in reverse chronological order, which I personally loved. […] Now, expired betas are scattered amongst active TestFlight betas, sorted alphabetically, and the expired list seems to have expanded to include every beta I've ever participated in. I roughly counted nearly 800 app entries for me. You can imagine active betas are few and far between in this list. The search helps, but there's no more scrolling to find anything.

Then in August, John Gruber wrote about the TestFlight update and bug over at Daring Fireball:

Last night, over a month after this bug appeared (and was flagged by Vorhees), Apple finally updated TestFlight for the first time. While the update notes mention only bug fixes, that's exactly what this update delivers.

TestFlight version 4.3.1 is the fix for users affected by this regression.
